We carry the WinterCraft WP72 (winter), Crugen HP71 (all-season SUV), Solus TA51a (all-season touring), and Road Venture AT52 (all-terrain) at 111 42 Ave SW.
settings.intro_heading: Why we recommend Kumho in Calgary
settings.intro_richtext:
Kumho has been making tires in South Korea since 1960. Among Calgary drivers they're known for excellent price-to-performance — particularly the WinterCraft winter line and the Crugen SUV all-season line.

The WinterCraft WP72 is Kumho's flagship passenger winter tire — directional tread pattern that channels slush and water on Calgary's wet-snow winter days. The Crugen HP71 is the SUV all-season most of our Calgary CR-V, RAV4, and Outback owners come back for.

For sedans wanting one tire all year, the Solus TA51a is a quiet, long-wearing all-season at an entry-level price. For trucks and SUVs that need 3PMSF certification, the Road Venture AT52 is the all-terrain pick.

Every Kumho we install gets the same balance, calibrated torque, and TPMS reset as our premium-priced jobs — and we price-match local Calgary competitors. Book installation or call (403) 452-4283.

settings.faq_1_q: Is Kumho a good tire brand?
settings.faq_1_a: Yes — Kumho is a tier-2 premium-adjacent Korean brand. Solid build quality, reliable warranty service, and noticeably better value than Michelin/Bridgestone equivalents. Best fit for Calgary drivers who want a quiet, long-lasting daily tire without paying top-tier prices.
settings.faq_2_q: What's the best Kumho tire for Calgary winters?
settings.faq_2_a: The WinterCraft WP72 for sedans and crossovers — directional tread pattern that handles wet snow and slush on Calgary's chinook freeze-thaw days. For trucks and bigger SUVs, the Road Venture AT52 carries 3PMSF certification.
settings.faq_3_q: How much do Kumho tires cost in Calgary?
settings.faq_3_a: Kumho tires at Prince Tires range from $140 to $380 per tire. Solus TA51a starts around $140; Crugen HP71 around $215; WinterCraft WP72 around $325; Road Venture AT52 around $375 in mid-range sizes.
settings.faq_4_q: Is the Road Venture AT52 3PMSF rated?
settings.faq_4_a: Yes. The Road Venture AT52 carries the 3PMSF (three-peak mountain snowflake) symbol — it meets Alberta's winter-tire law and the BC Highway 93 / Trans-Canada Banff winter-tire mandate from October 1 through April 30.
settings.faq_5_q: Crugen HP71 vs Solus TA51a — what's the difference?
settings.faq_5_a: Crugen HP71 is the SUV/crossover-tuned all-season — higher load ratings, slightly firmer sidewall for vehicle weight. Solus TA51a is the sedan/compact-car version — softer ride, lower load rating. Pick by vehicle type.
